questions.q: What do provider SDK packages like `openai` and `anthropic` do?
options: They train new AI models from scratch
They wrap a specific AI provider's API behind Python client/response/error objects
They replace the need for a virtual environment
They are only used for data visualization
questions.explain: Provider SDKs give you a Python-friendly client object, structured responses, and typed errors for one specific AI provider's API — the pattern covered in Lesson 16.

questions.q: Why does this course dedicate Chapter 5 specifically to the `requests` library rather than jumping straight to a provider SDK?
options: Because requests is the only library Python has
Because understanding raw HTTP, which requests handles, is what makes every provider SDK's behavior predictable instead of feeling like magic
Because provider SDKs don't actually use HTTP at all
Because requests is required to create a virtual environment
questions.explain: Every provider SDK is, underneath, making HTTP requests. Learning requests directly demystifies what those SDKs are actually doing on your behalf.

questions.q: Which category of library would `langchain` fall into, based on this lesson's groupings?
options: Provider SDK
HTTP library
Orchestration / application framework, for chaining multiple AI calls and tools together
Data & ML library
questions.explain: LangChain provides reusable pieces (prompt templates, memory, tool-calling helpers) for building multi-step AI applications, distinct from a single provider's SDK or a raw HTTP library.

questions.q: Which of these is a 'data & ML' library in this lesson's categorization, rather than a provider SDK or HTTP library?
options: openai
requests
anthropic
pandas
questions.explain: pandas handles tabular/structured data, placing it in the data & ML category alongside numpy, scikit-learn, and torch — distinct from provider SDKs (openai, anthropic) and the HTTP library (requests).

questions.q: What does `pip show requests` tell you?
options: It installs the requests library if it isn't already installed
It uninstalls requests
It prints requests' installed version, a summary, and related metadata
It opens requests' source code in a text editor
questions.explain: pip show prints details about an already-installed package — its version, summary, and location — without installing, uninstalling, or editing anything.
